extracted.subtask_description: Rules, primitives, and best practices for writing and debugging TeX macros, especially conditionals, expansion behavior, token lists, and I/O operations. Includes how various primitives expand and when expansion is suppressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: General conditional structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditionals have the general form \if(condition)(true text)\else(false text)\fi; the (false text) is optional and conditional constructions always end with a final \fi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The (true text) is skipped unless the condition is true, and the (false text) is skipped unless the condition is false. Use \else only when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional control sequence naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditional constructions begin with a control sequence whose first two letters are 'if' (for example \ifodd).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All conditionals begin with \if and have a matching \fi; this convention aids in visualizing nesting of conditionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ifnum (integer comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: \ifnum{number1}{relation}{number2} compares two integers; (relation) must be '<', '=', or '>'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to compare integer registers (e.g. \ifnum\balance=0). Be careful about following tokens: place a blank after numeric constants to terminate the number.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ifdim (dimension comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: \ifdim{dimen1}{relation}{dimen2} compares two dimensions (analogous to \ifnum for dimensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \ifdim\hsize>100pt.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ifodd (odd integer test)
rubrics_metrics.description: \ifodd{number} is true if the number is odd, false if even.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for alternating behavior (e.g. left/right page selection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode tests (\ifvmode, \ifhmode, \ifmmode, \ifinner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primitives to test TeX's current mode: \ifvmode (vertical), \ifhmode (horizontal), \ifmmode (math), \ifinner (internal mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return true when TeX is in the named mode (see Chapter 13 for mode details).

rubrics_metrics.name: \if token1 token2 (character-code comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: \if token1 token2 expands macros following \if until two unexpandable tokens are found; then the condition is true if the character codes agree (category codes ignored).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either token is a control sequence, it is considered to have character code 256 and category code 16 unless \let made it a nonactive character token. Be aware of expansion while searching for unexpandable tokens.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ifcat (category-code comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: \ifcat(token1)(token2) is like \if but tests whether the category codes of the two tokens agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active characters have category 13; use \noexpand{active character} to suppress expansion when testing such characters. Examples in text illustrate subtle uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ifx (token equivalence without expansion)
rubrics_metrics.description: \ifx(tok1)(tok2) compares the two tokens without expanding control sequences; true when tokens are identical as characters/primitives/fonts/defs or when macros have same status, parameters, and top-level expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to test whether two control sequences currently denote the same primitive or equivalent macros. The test does not expand the tokens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box-register tests (\ifvoid, \ifhbox, \ifvbox)
rubrics_metrics.description: \ifvoid{number}, \ifhbox{number}, \ifvbox{number} test box register content (number between 0 and 255).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True if the specified \box is void or contains an hbox / vbox respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ifeof (end-of-file test)
rubrics_metrics.description: \ifeof{number} is true unless the corresponding input stream (0..15) is open and not fully read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use after \openin; if file cannot be found, TeX treats stream as not open and \ifeof becomes true.

rubrics_metrics.name: \iftrue and \iffalse (predetermined outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: \iftrue and \iffalse are conditionals that are always true or always false respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are useful because they expand to proper conditional tokens (unlike earlier \yes/\no hacks) so nesting and skipping works correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ifcase (multi-way branching)
rubrics_metrics.description: \ifcase{number}(case0)\or(case1)\or ... \else(otherwise)\fi selects among n+1 cases separated by \or; \else is optional and handles out-of-range numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good for many-way branching based on integer value; number selects which text will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create boolean switches with \newif
rubrics_metrics.description: \newif\ifabc defines three control sequences: \ifabc (test), \abctrue, and \abcfalse. New conditionals are initially false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \newif to create named boolean switches (solves problems from using macros like \yes/\no).

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't \let\ifabc=\iftrue inside skipped text (caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid commands like \let\ifabc=\iftrue inside conditional text because if TeX skips that text it will miscount \if...\fi pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep such assignments buried inside macros so the \if... is only seen when not skipping; otherwise nesting matches go wrong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put a blank after numeric constants
rubrics_metrics.description: Always put a blank space after a numeric constant so TeX knows the constant is complete and does not expand following tokens into the number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing space can cause TeX to expand a following macro prematurely (possibly changing the number) and can cause subtle errors; the blank space is not output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Token-list registers and \toksdef / \newtoks
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX provides 256 token-list registers \toks0..\toks255 and \toksdef/\newtoks to name or allocate them; token lists can be reassigned or copied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Token list assignment syntax: (token variable)={(replacement text)} or (token variable)=(token variable). Token list registers behave like \everypar, \output, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracing and debugging macros (\tracingmacros, \tracingcommands, \tracingonline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set \tracingmacros=1 to see macro expansions; \tracingcommands=1 shows every command executed; \tracingcommands=2 shows conditional commands and outcomes; \tracingonline controls echoing to terminal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher values produce more diagnostic output (\tracingcommands>2 gives same as 2). Tracing info goes to the log file and/or terminal; useful to watch TeX in slow motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: When expansion is suppressed (list of contexts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expansion is suppressed in many situations: during error recovery; when skipping conditional text; when reading macro arguments; when reading control sequence names to be defined (\let, \futurelet, \def, \gdef, \edef, \xdef, \chardef, ...); when reading argument tokens for \expandafter, \noexpand, \string, \meaning, \let, \futurelet, \ifx, \show, \afterassignment, \aftergroup; when absorbing parameter or replacement text of \def/\gdef/\edef/\xdef or reading token variable text; when reading alignment preambles (except after \span or certain glue); just after $ or ' tokens used to begin math or alphabetic constants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list as a reference of contexts where tokens are not expanded; understanding these prevents surprises in macro behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macro-expansion process (macros)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a macro is expanded, TeX first determines its arguments (each argument is a token list and tokens are not expanded while being accepted), then replaces the macro and its arguments by the replacement text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macro expansion usually increases the number of tokens seen by later stages; be careful about where arguments are read to avoid unwanted expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional expansion behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: When an \if... is expanded TeX reads ahead as far as necessary to decide truth value; if false it skips ahead (tracking nesting) to the corresponding \else, \or, or \fi. The expansion of a conditional is empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditionals always reduce the number of tokens seen by later stages; treat conditionals as token-eliminating constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: \number primitive expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: \number{number} expands to the decimal representation of the number (preceded by - if negative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeX reads and expands tokens while parsing the number and then produces ASCII tokens representing the decimal digits (category code 12, except space is category 10).

rubrics_metrics.name: \romannumeral primitive expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: \romannumeral{number} expands to lowercase roman numerals; expansion is empty if number is zero or negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to produce roman numerals inline; expansion yields ASCII tokens.

rubrics_metrics.name: \string primitive expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: \string token reads the token without expansion; for control sequences it yields the control sequence name (taking \escapechar into account); otherwise yields the character token.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produces ASCII tokens (category code 12, space as 10). Useful to stringify tokens.

rubrics_metrics.name: \jobname primitive expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: \jobname expands to the name TeX chose for the job (e.g. 'paper' if output files paper.dvi and paper.log are used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produces ASCII tokens.

rubrics_metrics.name: \fontname primitive expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: \fontname{font} expands to the external file name corresponding to the font (e.g. 'cmr10'), including size information if not used at design size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expansion is a sequence of tokens representing the font name; a font can be specified by \font, \textfont, \scriptfont, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: \meaning primitive expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: \meaning token expands to the sequence of characters that would be displayed by \show on that token (e.g. 'macro:...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for debugging; yields ASCII tokens representing the meaning shown on the terminal.

rubrics_metrics.name: \csname ... \endcsname expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: \csname ... \endcsname reads and expands tokens up to \endcsname, then produces a single control sequence token corresponding to the name (defined like \relax if undefined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only character tokens should remain after reading; the result is a single control sequence usable in subsequent code.

rubrics_metrics.name: \expandafter behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: \expandafter reads the token immediately after it without expanding it (call it t), then reads the token after t (expanding it and any arguments), replaces that token by its expansion, and finally puts t back in front of that expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A powerful primitive for controlling expansion order; think of it as delaying expansion of the immediately following token until after the next token is expanded.

rubrics_metrics.name: \noexpand behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: \noexpand{token} yields the token itself as expansion but prevents that token from being expanded (it is treated as if its meaning were \relax during expansion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \noexpand to prevent expansion of a token during \edef or similar contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark-related expansions (\topmark, \firstmark, \botmark, \splitfirstmark, \splitbotmark)
rubrics_metrics.description: These primitives expand to the token list in the corresponding mark register (see Chapter 23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They produce token lists representing stored marks; useful in output routines and headers/footers.

rubrics_metrics.name: \input and \endinput behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: \input(file name) has null expansion but causes TeX to prepare to read from the specified file; \endinput has null expansion and causes TeX to stop reading from the file when the end of the current \input line is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If file cannot be found, TeX does not give an error message but treats the stream as not open; use \ifeof to test.

rubrics_metrics.name: \the (internal quantity) general behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: \the{internal quantity} expands to tokens representing the current value of a TeX variable (parameters, registers, codename values, special registers, fontdimen, hyphen/skewchar, lastpenalty/lastkern/lastskip, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many subcases: \the\count0, \the\skip255, \the\mathcode'/', \the\pagetotal, \the\fontdimen6\tenrm, \the\hyphenchar{font}, \the\lastpenalty, etc. Most results are ASCII tokens (category 12 except space) but some \the cases produce non-character tokens (e.g. font identifiers or token lists).

rubrics_metrics.name: \the{font} and \the{token variable}
rubrics_metrics.description: \the{font} produces a font identifier (e.g. \the\font gives the control sequence for current font). \the{token variable} produces a copy of the token list that is the current value of that variable (e.g. \the\everypar or \the\toks5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Token lists produced by \the are not expanded further when used in \edef contexts (special-case noted elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded definitions: \edef and \xdef semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: \edef and \xdef perform expanded definitions: TeX blindly expands the tokens of the replacement text according to expansion rules and then defines the control sequence to that expanded result (\xdef = \global\edef).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded definitions continue to expand tokens until only unexpandable tokens remain, except token lists produced by \the are not expanded further; use \noexpand to inhibit expansion of specific tokens. Conditionals in replacement text are evaluated during \edef.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlling partial expansion in \edef (\noexpand and \the / \toks trick)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can mix expanded and non-expanded pieces in an \edef by using \noexpand to prevent expansion of a following token or by placing tokens into a token register (\toks) and then using \the\toksN inside the \edef.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \edef\a{\b\noexpand\c\d} or \toks0={\c} \edef\a{\b\the\toks0\d} achieve different combinations of expansion levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitives that expand token lists similarly to \edef (\mark, \message, \errmessage, \special, \write)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands like \mark{...}, \message{...}, \errmessage{...}, \special{...}, and \write{number}{...} expand the token lists in braces almost exactly as \edef and \xdef do, except that a macro parameter character '#' should be doubled only in \edef but not in \mark etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The \write token list is read without expansion first; expansion occurs later when actually written to a file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading auxiliary files: \openin, \read, \closein
rubrics_metrics.description: \openin{number}=(file name) opens an auxiliary input stream (numbers 0..15). \read(number) to\cs reads the next line (or additional lines until braces balanced) into \cs as a parameterless macro (an empty line appended at EOF). \closein{number} closes the stream.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If file not found, TeX considers stream not open (no error); if \read number invalid or stream closed, input comes from terminal and TeX prompts unless number negative. \read macro definitions are local unless preceded by \global.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialog and user input with \message and \read
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \message{prompt} and \read to interact with the user; \read prints the macro name (e.g. \myname=) and waits for response, echoed to log file. Use \read-1 to suppress the printed prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can then post-process the read text (e.g. convert to uppercase) using macros; be aware that trailing return becomes a space unless handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loop construction \loop ... \repeat
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain TeX provides \loop o: \if... f/ ,3 \repeat where o: and ,3 are sequences of commands and \if... is any conditional test (without a matching \fi). TeX executes o:, if condition true executes f/ and repeats; when condition false loop stops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common idiom for simple loops. Example shows implementing a prompt loop that repeats until a Yes/No answer is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of \ifx for string comparisons in read loops
rubrics_metrics.description: When reading user input into a macro, test equality with predefined tokens using \ifx (e.g. \ifx\answer\yes) to determine accepted answers and set a \newif-based garbage flag as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines \read, \ifx, \newif, and \loop...\repeat to build robust input loops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded token lists from \the are ASCII with category codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Results of \number, \romannumeral, \string, \meaning, \jobname, \fontname and many \the cases are sequences of ASCII character tokens assigned category code 12 (other), except that character code 32 is given category 10 (space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of category codes of produced tokens when using them in later parsing/expansion contexts.
